provenance: The Halberd is an Aurelian heavy striker built around paired arm batteries and oversized cooling surfaces. Some recovered examples served with local missile cradles while their original emitters awaited replacement.
serviceHistory: Those early service refits made the difference between a valuable stored root and a machine that could earn its upkeep. Later work restored calibrated cooling and energy armament without always removing the practical local additions. A bright Halberd can therefore carry a thoroughly mixed maintenance history.

The tall shoulder pylons make an approaching Halberd easy to recognise. Freight guards learned not to assume that a heavy-looking contact would take a heavy machine's usual time to arrive. Custodian pilots take pride in that reputation; their workshops take equal care over the cooling surfaces that make repeated engagements affordable.
fieldNotes: The current standard pairs an Extended Arc Projector and Large Laser in each arm, with a central laser for close contacts. Compound cooling and reinforced plate support coordinated advances without ammunition bins. Keep the arms protected: losing one removes two primary weapons. Its stride helps a lance reposition, but there are no jump jets and a lone Halberd can lose a close duel to a well-equipped Bulwark.
